summary: Added docs/baseline/capability-inventory.json (98 public Client methods and 8 run.py flags, each with roadmap pillar, read-only/mutating/session kind, evidence level and citing tests) and capability-inventory.md (gaps per release R1-R6). Added tests/test_capability_inventory.py: it parses sdk/client.py and run.py with ast and fails on method or flag drift, unknown classifications, or cited tests that no longer mention the capability. Corrected the outdated offline-only roadmap sentence in README.template, then mirrored the change in README.md.

contract_status_changes.before: No inventory; README described the roadmap as offline-only
contract_status_changes.after: Versioned capability inventory with an ast-based drift test; README points to the full-gameplay research roadmap
proof: make test: 444 tests OK (1 skipped) on Python 3.13 .venv

residual_risks: Pillar and kind classifications were assigned by name-prefix rules and reviewed by hand; the drift test enforces parity and citations, not semantic correctness.
live-claimed entries (createBattle9, acceptBattle5, finaliseBattle15) restate README claims and were not re-verified against the current game version.
make lint runs uv run, which rewrites .venv and uv.lock; the CI ratchet (scripts/ci.py lint) was used instead and uv.lock was restored.
open_questions: The Makefile falls back to system python3 (3.9 here) when .venv is absent, so make test fails on machines without a project venv. Should make test bootstrap or require a venv?
